title: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 19 2024
description: Ethiopian English University Entrance Practice Test 19 2024 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: The research conference will begin ___ 8:30 ___ Monday morning.
questions.explanation: Use "at" for an exact time and "on" for a specific day.

questions.questionText: The students have been waiting ___ the professor ___ nearly an hour.
questions.explanation: "Wait for" identifies the person, while "for nearly an hour" expresses duration.

questions.questionText: She has lived in Addis Ababa ___ 2021 and has worked there ___ five years.
questions.explanation: "Since" takes a starting point; "for" takes a duration.

questions.questionText: The laboratory must be cleaned ___ Friday, but the equipment will remain there ___ Monday.
questions.explanation: "By Friday" gives a deadline, while "until Monday" means continuing up to Monday.

questions.questionText: The technician walked ___ the laboratory and placed the samples ___ the refrigerator.
questions.explanation: "Into" expresses movement inside; "in" expresses position inside.

questions.questionText: The hikers walked ___ the tunnel and then ___ the bridge to reach the village.
questions.explanation: Movement within a tunnel is "through"; movement from one side of a bridge to the other is "across".

questions.questionText: The temperature remained ___ zero throughout the night, while the blankets were placed ___ the sleeping bags.
questions.explanation: "Below" indicates a lower level; "over" indicates something positioned above or covering another thing.

questions.questionText: The village is located ___ the river and the mountain range, with a road running ___ the river.
questions.explanation: "Between" fits two distinct locations; "along" means following the length or direction of something.

questions.questionText: The manager stood ___ the entrance while the assistant waited ___ him.
questions.explanation: "In front of" indicates a position ahead of something; "behind" indicates a position at the back.

questions.questionText: The pharmacy is directly ___ the hospital, while the bank is ___ the school.
questions.explanation: "Opposite" means facing or directly across from; "beside" means next to.

questions.questionText: The students travelled ___ bus, but the researcher arrived ___ a taxi.
questions.explanation: Use "by bus" for means of transport and "in a taxi" for being inside a small vehicle.

questions.questionText: The passengers were already ___ the train when the announcement was made.
questions.explanation: "On" is commonly used when emphasizing being aboard a train.

questions.questionText: The surgeon removed the tissue ___ a small surgical instrument.
questions.explanation: "With" introduces the instrument or tool used.

questions.questionText: The report was sent ___ email and later delivered ___ hand to the director.
questions.explanation: "By email" expresses method; "by hand" is a fixed expression for method of delivery.

questions.questionText: The students discussed the consequences ___ the new policy ___ the examination system.
questions.explanation: "Consequences of" identifies what is affected, while "on" introduces the area affected.

questions.questionText: The package came ___ Nairobi and was addressed ___ the university library.
questions.explanation: "From" indicates origin; "to" indicates destination.

questions.questionText: The professor is highly ___ her students and is particularly ___ their progress.
questions.explanation: "Proud of" and "interested in" are fixed adjective-preposition combinations.

questions.questionText: Success in the competition will depend ___ how effectively the team works together.
questions.explanation: The verb "depend" is followed by "on".

questions.questionText: The students were asked to listen carefully ___ the instructions before beginning the experiment.
questions.explanation: The fixed combination is "listen to."

questions.questionText: The researcher apologized ___ arriving late ___ the meeting.
questions.explanation: "Apologize for" introduces the reason; "at" identifies the specific event or occasion.

questions.questionText: The students are deeply interested ___ learning how the experiment works.
questions.explanation: "Interested in" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The engineer is responsible ___ checking the equipment before each experiment.
questions.explanation: "Responsible for" is the standard combination.

questions.questionText: The two methods are similar ___ one another but different ___ their underlying assumptions.
questions.explanation: "Similar to" and "different from" are the standard combinations.

questions.questionText: The students were worried ___ the examination because they had not prepared adequately.
questions.explanation: "Worried about" means anxious concerning something.

questions.questionText: The professor was pleased ___ the students' progress but disappointed ___ their attendance.
questions.explanation: "Pleased with" is used for satisfaction; "disappointed about" can introduce the cause of disappointment.

questions.questionText: The students remained ___ the library ___ midnight to complete the project.
questions.explanation: "In the library" indicates location, while "until midnight" indicates the endpoint of their stay.

questions.questionText: The examination will be held ___ the morning ___ October 15.
questions.explanation: Use "in" with parts of the day and "on" with specific dates.

questions.questionText: The meeting has been scheduled ___ 10:00 ___ Tuesday.
questions.explanation: "At" is used for the exact time and "on" for the day.

questions.questionText: The university was established ___ 1950 and has operated continuously ___ that year.
questions.explanation: "In 1950" gives a year; "since that year" gives the starting point.

questions.questionText: The students have been working ___ three hours without taking a break.
questions.explanation: "For" is used with a duration.

questions.questionText: The students remained silent ___ the entire presentation.
questions.explanation: "During" means within the period of an event.

questions.questionText: Please submit your application ___ Friday; submissions received later will not be considered.
questions.explanation: "By Friday" establishes a deadline.

questions.questionText: The laboratory will remain closed ___ the safety inspection has been completed.
questions.explanation: "Until" means continuing up to the specified event.

questions.questionText: The keys were hidden ___ the drawer, directly ___ the documents.
questions.explanation: "In" indicates an enclosed space; "under" indicates a lower position.

questions.questionText: A large map was hanging ___ the wall directly ___ the professor's desk.
questions.explanation: "On the wall" describes surface contact; "above the desk" describes a higher position.

questions.questionText: The students gathered ___ the main entrance before walking ___ the building together.
questions.explanation: "At" identifies the meeting point; "into" expresses movement from outside to inside.

questions.questionText: The cyclist rode ___ the narrow street and then ___ the crowded marketplace.
questions.explanation: "Along" follows the length of a street; "through" describes movement within an area.

questions.questionText: The children ran ___ the field before walking ___ the road to the other side.
questions.explanation: "Across" can describe movement from one side of an open area or road to the other.

questions.questionText: The driver slowed down as he went ___ the school and continued ___ the main road.
questions.explanation: "Past" means moving beyond a place; "along" means following the direction or length of something.

questions.questionText: The cat jumped ___ the table and disappeared ___ the room.
questions.explanation: "Onto" indicates movement to a surface; "into" indicates movement inside.

questions.questionText: The plane flew ___ the mountains while the hikers walked ___ a narrow valley.
questions.explanation: "Over" indicates movement above something; "through" indicates movement within an enclosed or bounded passage.

questions.questionText: The temperature dropped ___ freezing point, while the aircraft remained ___ the clouds.
questions.explanation: "Below" expresses a lower level; "above" expresses a higher position.

questions.questionText: The new library is located ___ the science building and the administration block.
questions.explanation: "Between" is appropriate for two distinct locations.

questions.questionText: The researcher distributed the questionnaires ___ the participants gathered in the hall.
questions.explanation: "Among" is used when something is distributed within a group.

questions.questionText: The professor sat ___ the two students so that both could see the demonstration.
questions.explanation: "Between" is appropriate for two distinct people.

questions.questionText: The missing document was found ___ several old files in the archive.
questions.explanation: "Among" indicates being surrounded by or included within a group.

questions.questionText: The teacher stood ___ the students while the principal waited ___ the classroom door.
questions.explanation: "Among" fits a position within a group; "at" identifies a specific point.

questions.questionText: The students travelled ___ train, but the lecturer arrived ___ his private car.
questions.explanation: "By train" expresses means of transport; "in his car" describes being inside a vehicle.

questions.questionText: We usually travel ___ plane, but once we arrived ___ foot after the road was closed.
questions.explanation: The fixed expressions are "by plane" and "on foot."

questions.questionText: The passengers were waiting ___ the bus when the driver arrived ___ the station.
questions.explanation: "On the bus" means aboard it; "at the station" indicates a specific location.

questions.questionText: The child was sitting ___ the car while his parents waited ___ the entrance.
questions.explanation: "In the car" is standard for a small enclosed vehicle; "at the entrance" identifies a point.

questions.questionText: The company is famous ___ producing high-quality scientific equipment.
questions.explanation: "Famous for" introduces the reason for someone's or something's reputation.

questions.questionText: The final result was completely different ___ what the researchers had predicted.
questions.explanation: "Different from" is the standard combination taught in formal usage.

questions.questionText: The students were extremely good ___ solving complex mathematical problems.
questions.explanation: "Good at" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The organization is committed ___ improving educational opportunities in rural areas.
questions.explanation: "Committed to" is a fixed adjective-preposition combination, followed here by a gerund.

questions.questionText: The researcher is afraid ___ making the same mistake again.
questions.explanation: "Afraid of" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The students were proud ___ having completed the difficult project on time.
questions.explanation: "Proud of" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The committee is responsible ___ evaluating all applications before the deadline.
questions.explanation: "Responsible for" is the correct fixed combination.

questions.questionText: The decision depends ___ whether sufficient funding can be obtained.
questions.explanation: "Depend on" introduces the condition on which something relies.

questions.questionText: The old building belongs ___ the university and cannot be sold without permission.
questions.explanation: "Belong to" indicates ownership.

questions.questionText: The students agreed ___ the lecturer's interpretation of the results.
questions.explanation: "Agree with" is used when agreeing with a person or opinion.

questions.questionText: The committee agreed ___ a date for the final examination after several discussions.
questions.explanation: "Agree on" is used when reaching a decision about a particular matter.

questions.questionText: The students talked ___ the difficulties they had experienced during the experiment.
questions.explanation: "Talk about" means discuss a subject.

questions.questionText: The teacher asked the students to look ___ the diagram before answering the question.
questions.explanation: "Look at" is used when directing attention toward something.

questions.questionText: The passengers waited ___ the train for almost forty minutes.
questions.explanation: "Wait for" identifies the person or thing being awaited.

questions.questionText: The professor believes ___ giving students opportunities to conduct independent research.
questions.explanation: "Believe in" is used when expressing confidence in an idea, principle, or practice.

questions.questionText: The researcher apologized ___ not submitting the report before the deadline.
questions.explanation: "Apologize for" is followed by a noun or gerund describing the reason.

questions.questionText: The professor insisted ___ checking every calculation before publishing the results.
questions.explanation: "Insist on" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The students succeeded ___ completing the assignment despite the limited time available.
questions.explanation: "Succeed in" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The manager prevented the employees ___ entering the laboratory without permission.
questions.explanation: "Prevent someone from" is the standard construction.

questions.questionText: The researcher concentrated ___ identifying the main source of the error.
questions.explanation: "Concentrate on" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The students complained ___ the lack of adequate laboratory equipment.
questions.explanation: "Complain about" introduces the problem or issue causing dissatisfaction.

questions.questionText: The student complained ___ the supervisor that the examination instructions were unclear.
questions.explanation: "Complain to" identifies the person who receives the complaint.

questions.questionText: The researcher is accustomed ___ working under considerable pressure.
questions.explanation: "Accustomed to" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The students objected ___ changing the examination schedule at such short notice.
questions.explanation: "Object to" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The professor warned the students ___ relying entirely on memorization.
questions.explanation: "Warn against" means advise someone not to do something.

questions.questionText: The new evidence provides an explanation ___ the unexpected variation in the results.
questions.explanation: "An explanation for" identifies the thing being explained.

questions.questionText: The students were prevented ___ leaving the examination room before the scheduled time.
questions.explanation: "Prevented from" is followed by a gerund or noun.

questions.questionText: The researcher succeeded ___ obtaining reliable results after repeating the experiment.
questions.explanation: "Succeed in" is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: The professor was accused ___ ignoring important evidence during the investigation.
questions.explanation: "Accused of" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The students were prohibited ___ using calculators during the first section of the examination.
questions.explanation: "Prohibited from" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The university is committed ___ providing equal opportunities to all qualified applicants.
questions.explanation: "Committed to" is followed by a gerund when the next word is a verb.

questions.questionText: The final decision was based ___ evidence collected during the investigation.
questions.explanation: "Based on" is the standard combination.

questions.questionText: The researchers are capable ___ solving highly complex problems under pressure.
questions.explanation: "Capable of" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The students are familiar ___ the basic principles of organic chemistry.
questions.explanation: "Familiar with" means having knowledge of something.

questions.questionText: The researcher was satisfied ___ the accuracy of the final measurements.
questions.explanation: "Satisfied with" is the standard adjective-preposition combination.

questions.questionText: The committee is opposed ___ changing the regulations before the review is complete.
questions.explanation: "Opposed to" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The lecturer was concerned ___ the declining performance of first-year students.
questions.explanation: "Concerned about" means worried or troubled about something.

questions.questionText: The students were capable ___ completing the assignment without additional assistance.
questions.explanation: "Capable of" is followed by a gerund.

questions.questionText: The professor emphasized the importance ___ checking the data before drawing conclusions.
questions.explanation: "Importance of" is followed here by a gerund.

questions.questionText: The students were unable to agree ___ which method would produce the most reliable results.
questions.explanation: "Agree on" is used when reaching a decision about a particular matter.

questions.questionText: The lecturer referred ___ several studies to support her argument.
questions.explanation: "Refer to" means mention or direct attention to a source.

questions.questionText: The researcher compared the new findings ___ those reported in the earlier study.
questions.explanation: "Compare with" is commonly used when examining similarities and differences between two things.

questions.questionText: The manager provided the interns ___ detailed instructions before the experiment began.
questions.explanation: "Provide someone with something" is the standard construction.

questions.questionText: The final result was contrary ___ what the researchers had initially expected.
questions.explanation: "Contrary to" means opposite to something.

questions.questionText: The students had difficulty ___ understanding the lecturer's explanation.
questions.explanation: "Have difficulty with" is followed here by the activity being difficult.

questions.questionText: The researcher insisted ___ repeating the experiment before accepting the conclusion.
questions.explanation: "Insist on" is followed by a noun or gerund.

questions.questionText: The students were excited ___ participating in the national competition.
questions.explanation: "Excited about" is used to express enthusiasm concerning something.

questions.questionText: The professor was annoyed ___ the students for failing to follow the instructions.
questions.explanation: "Annoyed with someone" identifies the person causing irritation.

questions.questionText: The professor was annoyed ___ the repeated interruptions during the lecture.
questions.explanation: "Annoyed about" can identify the thing causing irritation.
